title: Finite-ring compact-support site comparisons respect refinements and towers
statement:
Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring. Work on ordinary constant-$R$ module derived categories of the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let all schemes be Noetherian, meaning they admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings. For a compactifiable separated finite-type map $h:U\to V$, choose $c=(j:U\hookrightarrow W,r:W\to V)$ and put $F_h^{t,c}=Rr_*^t j_!^t$ on site $t$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] [def-asd-compactifiable]. Write $N_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and define $C_h^c=Rr_*^{\rm pro}(e_j)\circ d_r(j_!^{\rm et}(-))$, using the canonical open comparison $e_j$ and proper counit mate $d_r$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. For $E\in D^+(U_{\rm et},R)$ the map $C_h^c$ is invertible. For a proper refinement $u$ of $c$ by $c'$ let $\rho^t:F_h^{t,c}\to F_h^{t,c'}$ be the normalized proper-refinement comparison, the direct image of the proper/open refinement map $\alpha_u$ of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison] on the etale site and of its pro-etale counterpart $\alpha_u^{\rm pro}$ of [lem-sp-refinement-coefficient-mate] on etale-origin pro-etale objects. For the composition assertion let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be composable compactifiable separated finite-type maps of Noetherian schemes, choose compactifications of $f$, $g$ and $gf$, and let $\alpha^t:F_g^tF_f^t\to F_{gf}^t$ be the normalized composition through compatible compactification towers [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. On etale-origin pro-etale objects use the corresponding proper/open pastes, with the pro-etale interchange $\Gamma^{\rm pro}$ of [lem-sp-proper-open-coefficient-mate]. Then
$$ C_h^{c'}\circ N_V(\rho^{\rm et})=\rho^{\rm pro}N_U\circ C_h^c,$$
$$ C_{gf}N_Z(\alpha^{\rm et})=\alpha^{\rm pro}N_X\circ F_g^{\rm pro}(C_f)\circ C_g(F_f^{\rm et}(-)).$$
Thus the computed pro-etale proper/open comparisons coincide with transport through $C$. These equations hold through every common refinement, and respect identity maps and associativity. They are natural in $E$ and impose no special coefficient presentation or assumption that the base field is algebraically closed. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tags 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined) and 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition). Agent site-coherence deduction using the separately stated refinement and interchange site equations.

proof.text: All comparisons are evaluated on bounded-below etale complexes. Exactness of the two open-extension functors and of $N$ implies that they preserve cohomological lower bounds. Consequently the sheaf comparison $e_j$ induces the indicated derived comparison termwise; its composition equation also descends termwise, since the exact functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. The etale derived direct image has codomain $D^+$, so every etale intermediate $Rr_*j_!E$, including the input to $C_g$, is bounded below. For each proper map used below the source and target are Noetherian, hence the target is quasi-separated and the source is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The qcqs permanence lemma therefore supplies the hypotheses of the specified direct-image counit-mate comparison $d_r$. Its invertibility and that of $e_j$ make $C_h^c=Rr_*^{\rm pro}(e_j)\circ d_r(j_!^{\rm et}(-))$ an invertible natural transformation. Moreover $F_h^{\rm pro}N_UE$ is of bounded-below etale origin, with witness $(F_h^{\rm et}E,C_h^c(E))$. This supplies each subsequent pro-etale input; no unrestricted preservation assertion on arbitrary pro-etale complexes is needed.

Use the canonical direct-image compositors $\kappa^t_{b,a}:Rb_*^tRa_*^t\xrightarrow{\sim}R(ba)_*^t$. Their adjunction normalization follows from the derived-composition normalization lemma applied to the exact constant-ring inverse images and their right adjoints. Its Grothendieck hypotheses hold by the module-sheaf theorem for small sites: a sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf is equivalently a sheaf of $R$-modules, since the action of a locally constant scalar is uniquely obtained by gluing its constant local actions. Exactness and the adjunctions are supplied by the etale inverse-image theorem and the pro-etale operations. The site pullback comparisons $a_a,a_b,a_{ba}$ respect composition. Since $d$ is exactly their inverse-square counit mate, part (2) of mate pasting, with the normalized composite adjunctions, and part (3) to pass between the composite adjunction and that of $ba$ along these compositors, gives
$$d_{ba}\circ N(\kappa^{\rm et}_{b,a})=(\kappa^{\rm pro}_{b,a}N)\circ Rb_*^{\rm pro}(d_a)\circ d_b(Ra_*^{\rm et}(-)).$$
This is a specialization of the cited pasting identity, not a choice of $d_{ba}$. Its identity case is part (4) of the same lemma. The open counterpart is the composition equation for $e$ from Step 1, with the canonical $J_bJ_a\cong J_{ba}$ inserted. Here and below $P_r^t=Rr_*^t$ and $J_j^t=j_!^t$, and canonical associators are inserted in every word of functors.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), second equality; Mathlib mateEquiv_hcomp for the site deduction

proof.text:
Orient a refinement as $u:W_1\to W_2$, $u j_1=j_2$, $r_1=r_2u$, so $c=(j_2,r_2)$, $c'=(j_1,r_1)$. By the specified normalization,
$$\rho^t=\kappa^t_{r_2,u}(J_{j_1}^t(-))\circ P_{r_2}^t(\alpha_u^t).$$
The site clause of the refinement-mate lemma gives
$$P_u^{\rm pro}(e_{j_1})\circ d_u(J_{j_1}^{\rm et}(-))\circ N(\alpha_u^{\rm et})=\alpha_u^{\rm pro}N\circ e_{j_2}.$$
Apply $P_{r_2}^{\rm pro}$ to this equality. In $C_h^{c'}N(\rho^{\rm et})$, substitute the formula for $\rho$, replace $d_{r_2u}N\kappa^{\rm et}$ by Step 2, and use naturality of $\kappa^{\rm pro}$ to move $e_{j_1}$ past it. Naturality of $d_{r_2}$ moves $N(\alpha_u^{\rm et})$ next to $d_u$. The displayed refinement equation then replaces these inner three factors by $\alpha_u^{\rm pro}N\circ e_{j_2}$. The outside factors are exactly $\kappa^{\rm pro}_{r_2,u}P_{r_2}^{\rm pro}(\alpha_u^{\rm pro})$ followed by $P_{r_2}^{\rm pro}(e_{j_2})d_{r_2}(J_{j_2}^{\rm et}(-))$, giving
$$C_h^{c'}\circ N_V(\rho^{\rm et})=\rho^{\rm pro}N_U\circ C_h^c.$$
The original refinement square is not required to be Cartesian.

source.place: Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined), comparison along a morphism of compactifications; site clause of lem-sp-refinement-coefficient-mate

proof.text:
First compute composition on a compatible tower. Use the tower lemma to choose $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, $q:\overline Y\to Z$, $a:X\hookrightarrow U$, $b:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $s:U\to Y$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, with $pb=is$ Cartesian, $p,s,q$ proper, $f=sa$, and $gf=(qp)(ba)$. Thus the tower candidates are $F_f^t=P_s^tJ_a^t$, $F_g^t=P_q^tJ_i^t$, $F_{gf}^t=P_{qp}^tJ_{ba}^t$. By the normalization clause of the unbounded compact-support comparison theorem, whose comparisons restrict on bounded-below inputs to those of the etale compactification comparison theorem, the etale composition on this tower is precisely
$$P_q^tJ_i^tP_s^tJ_a^t\xrightarrow{P_q^t(\Gamma^t J_a^t)}P_q^tP_p^tJ_b^tJ_a^t\xrightarrow{\kappa^t_{q,p},\,m^t_{b,a}}P_{qp}^tJ_{ba}^t,$$
where $m^t_{b,a}:J_b^tJ_a^t\cong J_{ba}^t$ is open composition. On the pro-etale site this uses the specified open adjunct $\Gamma^{\rm pro}$, not an isomorphism chosen by conjugation with $C$. The Cartesian square is exactly one to which the site clause of the proper/open-mate lemma applies. Its input is the bounded-below complex $J_a^{\rm et}E$, and Step 1 identifies $J_a^{\rm pro}N_XE$ with its etale-origin pullback.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), compatible tower and four displayed equalities

proof.text:
For this tower the site equation for $\Gamma$, evaluated at $J_a^{\rm et}E$, is
$$P_p^{\rm pro}(e_b)\circ d_p(J_b^{\rm et}(-))\circ N(\Gamma^{\rm et})=\Gamma^{\rm pro}N\circ J_i^{\rm pro}(d_s)\circ e_i(P_s^{\rm et}(-)).$$
Whisker this equality on the right by $J_a^{\rm et}$ and on the left by $P_q^{\rm pro}$. To its domain attach $d_q(J_i^{\rm et}P_s^{\rm et}J_a^{\rm et}E)$; naturality of $d_q$ identifies the top route with $N_Z$ of the first arrow in Step 4 followed by the comparisons for the resulting word. To its codomain attach $P_q^{\rm pro}P_p^{\rm pro}J_b^{\rm pro}(e_a(E))$. Naturality of $\Gamma^{\rm pro}$ moves this last $e_a$ across $\Gamma^{\rm pro}$, so the bottom route becomes
$$P_q^{\rm pro}J_i^{\rm pro}(C_f(E))\circ C_g(F_f^{\rm et}E)$$
followed by the pro-etale tower interchange. These are equal maps from $N_ZP_q^{\rm et}J_i^{\rm et}P_s^{\rm et}J_a^{\rm et}E$ to $P_q^{\rm pro}P_p^{\rm pro}J_b^{\rm pro}J_a^{\rm pro}N_XE$. This explicitly pastes the named interchange square and the open comparison, using only naturality.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open) and 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition); site-square pasting in the compatible tower

proof.text:
Postcompose the equality of Step 5 with the pro-etale compositors $\kappa^{\rm pro}_{q,p}$ and $m^{\rm pro}_{b,a}$. Apply the proper and open comparison equations of Step 2 to these two adjacent factors. They replace comparison for the word $P_qP_pJ_bJ_a$ after the etale compositors by $C_{gf}$ for $P_{qp}J_{ba}$. The etale interchange followed by the etale compositors is $\alpha^{\rm et}$ by Step 4; the corresponding pro-etale factors are $\alpha^{\rm pro}$. The result is exactly
$$C_{gf}\circ N_Z(\alpha^{\rm et})=\alpha^{\rm pro}N_X\circ F_g^{\rm pro}(C_f)\circ C_g(F_f^{\rm et}(-)).$$
This is an equality for the computed normalized arrows. In particular their agreement with transport through $C$ is a conclusion: solve this equation for $\alpha^{\rm pro}N_X$, using the inverse of $F_g^{\rm pro}(C_f)\circ C_g(F_f^{\rm et}(-))$. The refinement equation similarly solves for $\rho^{\rm pro}N_U$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), assembly of the tower formula; substitution of Steps 2, 4, 5

proof.text: For arbitrary compactifications compare them with the tower choices using a common proper refinement; such refinements and common refinements of towers exist by the cited geometric lemmas. The etale refinement maps are coherent isomorphisms and the etale composition is independent of the tower: this is the etale compactification comparison theorem, applied to the proper/open tower composition of Step 4, which by the unbounded compact-support comparison theorem is its composition map restricted to bounded-below inputs. Step 3 expresses every computed pro-etale refinement map as $C^{c'}N(\rho^{\rm et})(C^c)^{-1}$; hence its identity, composition, and common-refinement independence follow by cancelling adjacent $C^{-1}C$ and using the etale equalities. The same holds for a comparison through a common refinement, since it is a composite of a refinement comparison and an inverse. In the tower identity of Step 6 replace each tower candidate by its comparison with the chosen candidate. Step 3 commutes the $C$ factors past these comparisons; naturality commutes $C_g$ past the comparison on $F_f^{\rm et}E$. The etale square for changing tower commutes by choice independence, and all remaining comparison isomorphisms cancel. This proves Step 6 for the chosen compactifications and shows that every common refining tower gives the same pro-etale composition map.

source.place: Tags 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined) and 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), independence of common refinements and towers

proof.text:
The open comparison at the identity is the identity under the canonical unit identifications: its composition equation with two identity opens makes it an invertible idempotent. The proper comparison at the identity is the identity by Step 2. Thus $C_{\mathrm{id}}$ is normalized to the identity. For three maps $f,g,h$, both pro-etale composition parenthesizations equal
$$C_{hgf}\circ N(\alpha^{\rm et}_{\rm triple})\circ D^{-1},\qquad D=F_h^{\rm pro}F_g^{\rm pro}(C_f)\circ F_h^{\rm pro}(C_gF_f^{\rm et})\circ C_h(F_g^{\rm et}F_f^{\rm et}).$$
Indeed substitute Step 6 twice into either parenthesization; naturality of $C_h$ and of the composition maps moves the inner $C$ factors together and cancels them, leaving exactly the displayed three-factor $D$. The two etale triple maps agree by etale associativity, proving pro-etale associativity; the same cancellation with an identity gives the unit laws. Each constituent $d,e,\rho^{\rm et},\Gamma^{\rm et},\Gamma^{\rm pro}$ is natural, so the pasted equations are natural in $E$. Throughout we used an arbitrary finite commutative $R$ and Noetherian schemes, with neither a coefficient presentation nor a hypothesis on a base field.
